contradicted: THE FALSIFIER THAT MATTERS IS F2, AND IT IS THE ONE A PLAUSIBLE WRONG FIX FAILS. The rail's own status for 48453:134392 is `present`, and the SERVED state is `conflicting`. A naive 'forward what the rail says' implementation passes F1 (present) and F3 (absent) and FAILS F2 -- it would print a present ring beside city limits that say incorporated, which is the exact contradiction the panel exists to surface. The test asserts `not.toBe('present')` AND `not.toBe('unresolved')` BEFORE asserting `toBe('conflicting')`, so verbatim forwarding cannot pass it. Separately, the two fixture parcels' PRE files are the control: had the change moved a state it does not claim to move, the PRE/POST pair would differ in a row the change never touches, and the byte-for-byte unslated assertion (F5a/b/c) is the same control in the suite. WHAT WOULD CONTRADICT THIS CLOSE: (a) an unslated county's PDF rendering anything other than the pre-change sentence byte for byte; (b) a `not-applicable` cell rendering the checked-absence sentence; (c) the etjStatus rail's real P-336 cell shape falling outside the set CP1's `railCellContract` enumerates -- the reader would then REFUSE rather than guess, which is the designed behaviour but still means this close's `conflicting` render is unproven against the live payload; (d) P-331's drift check finding the engine's resolveEtjDetermination diverging from the panel's behaviour matrix.

missionPremise: P-332 (hauska-map #419, live on Property Explorer m6wqid8u7) made the PANEL serve a four-state ETJ determination -- present / absent / unresolved / conflicting, where `conflicting` is city limits reading `incorporated` beside an ETJ read of `present`, which disagree by definition because a Texas ETJ is unincorporated land outside city limits. The PDF and the site-plan report kept saying `unresolved` for every parcel because the engine WROTE THE ANSWER AS A LITERAL (`report-model.ts:1304` at c41a1482, `JurisdictionFacts.etjStatus` typed as the literal "unresolved" at `feasibility-model.ts:209`), with comments asserting no engine ETJ source exists. The dispatch's ruling is therefore: the engine must READ the same `etjStatus` rail the panel reads and forward the determination, never derive ETJ from city limits and never read cortex's facets (P-332's rule 3) -- 'the PDF says what the panel says about ETJ'. Two premises the work rests on and did not re-litigate: (1) the `etjStatus` rail is already declared on both sides and is the intended serving path (rail-keys.ts:43; retrieval-api's parcel-record-rail-registry.ts:54), with P-336 in flight as its writer; (2) CODE-DONE != CUSTOMER-DONE (canon preamble) -- a merged PR is not the grade, a live probe on the deployed surface across different-data parcels is, which is why this close declares `customerDone: false` and names the probe rather than claiming the row finished.
completionPredicate: STRANGER-EVALUABLE FORM: P-358 is done when, on the DEPLOYED surface and after P-336's cells are applied, running `node --use-system-ca scripts/surface-probe.mjs` in doc_repo with the PDF leg on parcels 48453:134392 and 48209:97658 reads the SAME ETJ state the Property Explorer panel reads for the same parcels -- `conflicting` (both readings and both sources stated) for 48453:134392 and `absent` (with the ring count) for 48209:97658 -- and a county whose rail is unslated still renders the pre-change `unresolved` sentence. THIS LANE'S OWN PREDICATE is the strictly weaker, in-process one it could actually measure: the four states render correctly through `composeParcelReportFacts -> emitPdfFeasibility`, an unslated/refused/failed rail renders `unresolved` with its reason and the pre-change sentence byte for byte, the pre-change code renders `unresolved` for all ten fixtures (shown by revert-and-run), and `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm test` are green on the head commit in CI. Both predicates are stated because the dispatch forbids this lane from running the stronger one.

IN SCOPE: hauska-engine only (the dispatch: 'You build in hauska-engine only and open one PR'); the model, the rail read, the composition, the two PDF rows, the two narrative sentences, the exports, and tests. OUT BY THE DISPATCH'S OWN WORDS: merging, deploying, and building production PDFs ('the integration seat does'); the `etjStatus` ledger cells themselves (P-336 writes them -- this lane is the READER); the cross-repo drift check (P-331 owns it; this lane exports the literals and the behaviour matrix it needs); cortex's facets (P-332 rule 3 forbids reading them). threeQuestionGate.whatExecutesTheEtjStateOnThePdf: resolveEtjDetermination in packages/engine-core/src/site-plan/etj-determination.ts -- ONE implementation, called ONCE from report-model.ts's composeParcelReportFacts. It takes (the engine's city-limits reading, the etjStatus rail's answer, the unslated fallback reason) and returns the four-state determination plus the carried fact, the declared conflict and the reason. pdf/feasibility.ts's etjFactChip/etjConsequenceSentence and report-model.ts's jurisdictionActionSentence/jurisdictionSkeletonSentence only READ the composed model; none of them re-derives a state. The rail answer itself comes from recordEtjStatusAnswer (parcel-record-reader-client.ts), which reuses the P-302 recordRailAnswer three-way rule.
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggersIt: The retrieval service's `etjStatus` rail -- already declared on both sides (engine-core/src/parcel-record/rail-keys.ts:43, retrieval-api's parcel-record-rail-registry.ts:54), reading `excluded-mid-cutover` today, written by P-336. For a parcel whose rail serves `record`, the cell's value/absence kind decides the reading: a state string, a determination object, a declared conflict object, or an `absent-verified` cell (promoted to ETJ `absent`). Everything else -- an unslated rail, a refusal, `not-applicable`, a malformed payload, no reader at all, a failed fetch -- resolves to `unresolved` WITH a reason, and the three 'no determination in hand at all' paths render the pre-change sentence byte for byte so no county's document changes before P-336 applies.
threeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenThePdfAndThePanelDisagree: TODAY: nothing -- that WAS the defect. What this lane ADDS: (a) the PDF no longer asserts a state it does not have, so a parcel whose rail has not answered says `unresolved` + why rather than a fabricated present/absent; (b) within the engine's own surfaces the PDF and the narrative read ONE composed value, so the fact sheet and the narrative cannot disagree with each other -- before this lane they could only agree because both were the same literal; (c) a declared conflict is a SERVED STATE rather than a hidden disagreement, so `incorporated` + `present` cannot be printed as a clean pair; (d) the cross-repo agreement is a named, exported literal set plus a behaviour matrix for P-331's drift check. WHAT STILL DOES NOT FAIL, SAID PLAINLY: nothing in the engine compares its own read against the panel's LIVE read, and the rail's writer is P-336 -- so a ledger cell that is WRONG (rather than unreadable) is forwarded as-is. That is deliberate: P-332's rule 3 says the determination is read, never derived, and which of two disagreeing reads is wrong for a live conflict is a STORE question that etj-determination.ts's header deliberately does not decide in code.
threeQuestionGate.whatBypassesIt: Named rather than assumed. (a) The MCP / card / share surfaces in hauska-map -- P-332 shipped the panel's four states and P-336 makes the cells serve; the PDF is now the THIRD surface reading the same rail, and the probe in `probe.theProbeForAfterP336` is what checks the agreement after the deploy. (b) cortex-api's narrative path -- the jurisdiction object is SPREAD into the LDT narrative payload, so the new fields ride along inside an object that was already sent; whether cortex tolerates the extra keys is NOT measured by this lane (no deploy, no live call) and is named in openAtCP2. (c) Any OTHER engine surface rendering jurisdiction -- bounded by the census: the token appears in exactly six production sites and ONE PDF row prints ETJ. (d) The two named harness bypasses that apply to the doc_repo gates generally: a commit made outside the harness, and a close that declares `spawned: 0` falsely -- the fan-depth gate reads the declaration and cannot see a Cursor session's sub-agents, which is why this close declares honestly instead.
